Guidance & outlook: Suppliers Cost of materials consumed rose from ₹4,873.13 lakh to ₹6,239.29 lakh during the year - the single largest driver of margin pressure, and a reminder of how closely the Company's fortunes are tied to its raw -material VINNY OVERSEAS LIMITED 34th Annual Report · FY 2025-26 supply chain.

Basic and diluted earnings per share for the year were ₹0.02, against ₹0.14 in FY 2024-25 - a decline that mir rors the fall in net profit and is explained in full in the financial highlights that follow.

The details of complaints relating to sexual harassment during the financial year 2025-26 are as under: a) number of complaints pending as on beginning of FY2026: Nil b) number of complaints of sexual harassment received in FY2026: Nil c) number of complaints disposed off during FY2026: NA d) number of cases pending for more than ninety days: NA MANAGEMENT D…
Growth & demand: Revenue from operations grew 2.50%, from ₹121.57 crore to ₹124.62 crore, evidence that our customer relationships and job-processing capacity held firm through a competitive year.
Total assets grew from ₹106.09 crore to ₹124.21 crore over the year, and net worth strengthened from ₹82.18 crore to ₹83.00 crore.

On the other, cost of materials consumed rose by ₹1,366.15 lakh year-on-year, and depreciation and amortisation rose from ₹505.41 lakh to ₹600.43 lakh, reflecting continued investment in plant, machinery and equipment, which grew in gross book value from ₹2,865.02 lakh to ₹4,222.55 lakh over the year.
Margins & costs: For Vinny Overseas Limited, FY 2025-26 was a year of exactly that kind of interweaving: of people who kept the plant running, customers who kept placing orders even as input costs rose, a Board that renewed its independent oversight, and an organisation th at held its revenue line steady even as margins came under pressure.

At the same time, profitability came under real pressure: profit after tax fell from ₹5.15 crore to ₹0.92 crore, driven chiefly by a rise in the cost of materials consumed and depreciation, and by the tapering -off of a one -time Gujarat Textile Policy subsidy that had lifted other income in the prior year.

The Board has approved a remuneration of ₹54,000 (Rupees Fifty Four Thousand only), plus applicable taxes and reimbursement of out- of-pocket expenses, payable to the Cost Auditor for conducting the aforesaid cost audit.
Capex & expansion: Resilience, this year, meant discipline rather than dramatic reinvention: holding customer relationships, keeping the plant running through machinery -level energy -saving measures, strengthening the Board's independent oversight through the re-appointment of two Independent Directors, and continuing to invest in property, plant and equipment even as margins…

Innovation this year showed up instead at the process level - in energy-conscious operating discipline (detailed in Sustainable Fabric, below) and in the continued modernisation of plant and machinery, where gross additions took the block from ₹2,865.02 lakh to ₹4,222.55 lakh.

STRENGTH OF PEOPLE Human Capital, Skill Development, Safety Employee benefits expense rose from ₹490.38 lakh to ₹625.39 lakh during the year - a 27.5% increase that reflects both wage growth and continued investment in the workforce even as overall profitability came under pressure.
Balance sheet & cash: Trade payables turnover stood at 6.17 times against 7.00 times last year, reflecting a modest lengthening of the payment cycle as the Company managed working capital through the year.
The Board has, with a view to conserving resources for the business, not recommended a dividend for the year.

As per Section 124 of the Act, the amount of dividend for the subsequent years remaining unpaid or uncla imed for a period of seven years from the date of transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account of the Company shall be transferred to the IEPF.
Risks & challenges: The major relevant risk include increase in price of input materials, market risk, oversight in estimation and other major areas in risk management inclu des process of estimation, contract management and timely decision - making process.

RISK MANAGEMENT POLICY LEGAL FRAMEWORK VINNY OVERSEAS LIMITED 34th Annual Report · FY 2025-26 Risk Management is a key aspect of the “Corporate Governance Principles and Code of Conduct” which aims to improvise the governance practices across the Company's activities.

Our audit of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements included obtaining an understanding of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk.
